questions.q: What is an architecture decision record (ADR), according to this lesson?
options: A live dashboard tracking every open governance ticket
A legal contract between two business units
A quarterly budget spreadsheet
A short, dated document capturing one specific decision — context, decision, and consequences
questions.explain: An ADR is a short, historical record of one specific decision, written once and rarely edited afterward.

questions.q: What happens, per this lesson, when a decision captured in an ADR later changes?
options: The old ADR is deleted permanently with no trace
The original ADR is edited in place to reflect the new decision
The change gets its own new ADR rather than editing the old one
Nothing is recorded — ADRs are never updated for changes
questions.explain: The lesson states a later change gets a new ADR, with the old one marked Superseded, rather than editing history.

questions.q: Which four fields make up the standard ADR shape this lesson describes?
options: Budget, Timeline, Owner, Vendor
Risk, Reward, Probability, Cost
Title, Font, Color, Logo
Status, Context, Decision, Consequences
questions.explain: Status, Context, Decision, and Consequences (alongside a title) make up the standard ADR shape shown in the lesson's template.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say governance architecture especially benefits from ADRs?
options: ADRs are legally required for all governance programs
Governance decisions are never significant enough to document
It's full of expensive-to-reverse, constantly second-guessed decisions like operating model and platform choice
Governance teams are not allowed to use any other documentation format
questions.explain: The lesson lists operating model choice, platform selection, policy enforcement location, and security boundaries as prime ADR candidates.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about a decision with no stated downside in its Consequences section?
options: It means the decision requires no ADR at all
It means the decision was definitely correct
It usually has a downside that just went unexamined
It means the ADR should be deleted
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns that an ADR with no stated cost almost always has one that simply wasn't examined.
